deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The notes study arrangements (systems) of pseudolines in the real projective plane. They focus on the 'relative position' of one pseudoline L with respect to the others and on how that position changes under elementary moves.

Picture conventions. In the coloured figures the green circle is L̃, the 'structural polygon' of L. It is the double (antipodal) cover of L, drawn as the boundary of a disc, as if L were the line at infinity. Its vertices are the 2n endpoints of the other pseudolines (orange chords), which meet the circle in antipodal pairs. The orange shaded regions are the triangular cells of the arrangement that have a side on L.

Arcs on L̃. The previous page cut L̃ at the 'transition vertices' into three kinds of arcs:
(a) generalization arcs;
(b) specialization arcs, ordinary or exceptional;
(c) arcs of inaction/inertia.
The sides of the resulting 'characteristic polygons' are the 'characteristic arcs'.

First half of this page: a technical normalisation.
- An arc of inertia whose endpoints are endpoints of an exceptional specialization arc is called (by abuse) an exceptional inertia arc.
- Grothendieck then proposes to 'retract' each exceptional specialization arc, so that it stops slightly before its primitive endpoints, at the 'constitutive' critical points.
- Gain: all transition arcs become pairwise disjoint in every case. Two adjacent retracted characteristic arcs then share exactly one endpoint, so no exceptional cases need separate treatment.
- This is a general-position / regularisation trick that turns the decomposition of L̃ into an honest polygon subdivision.

Second half: the elementary move.
- A generalization arc a on L̃ lies between the endpoints of two lines D, D' bounding a triangle adjacent to L. Its antipodal copy is treated simultaneously.
- The move 'crushes the arms' of a: L is pushed across the vertex D∩D'. It passes through the non-simple configuration where L, D and D' are concurrent (hatched middle disc; the 'X' figure with the line passing through the crossing).
- It comes out on the other side. The order of D and D' along L is reversed (labels D D' become D' D), and the triangle reappears on the opposite side.
- This is exactly a triangle flip (Ringel mutation, Reidemeister-III-type move). Under it, the generalization arc a of L corresponds to a specialization arc a' of the new pseudoline L'.
- The combinatorial structure of L̃ is otherwise unchanged.

View from the space X. In the space X of configurations, with discriminant Σ (the walls of non-simple configurations), the move is seen as an 'anti-sweep'. A wall s of Σ slides in the direction of the generalization arc, which 'pushes' on L, and produces the corresponding specialization arc on the next position.

Gluing the polygons. When (L,a) and (L',a') correspond, Grothendieck proposes gluing the polygons Δ_L and Δ_{L'} by identifying a with a'. The next page decides that the right identification is the symmetry exchanging s and t, hence D with D'. This is the opposite of the tautological transport isomorphism. With it, all faces of the resulting 2-complex are quadrilaterals, dual to the graph of relative positions, giving a 'semi-circularisation' of that graph.

Purpose. The page serves to build a cellular (2-dimensional) model of the space of relative positions of a pseudoline and of the flip graph of arrangements.
errors: The terminology generalization/specialization is somewhat confusing: 'crushing the arms' of an arc is itself a passage to a special (concurrent) position, followed by re-generalization. Grothendieck's labels refer to the arcs as origin and target of the move, not to the intermediate step.
The retraction of exceptional arcs is only sketched: where exactly the 'constitutive critical extremities' lie is not defined on this page.

ideas.what: Structural polygon L̃ of a pseudoline: antipodal double cover of L with vertices the crossings with the other lines.
ideas.modern_name: local sequence / cyclic order of crossings on a pseudoline; boundary of the affine chart with L at infinity

ideas.what: Triangle flip: L slides through the vertex D∩D' via a triple point, reversing the order of D and D' on L and moving the adjacent triangle to the other side.
ideas.modern_name: mutation / triangle flip (Ringel), Reidemeister III move, wall-crossing in the discriminant of arrangements

ideas.what: Retracting exceptional specialization arcs so that transition arcs are pairwise disjoint and adjacent characteristic arcs meet in exactly one point.
ideas.modern_name: regularisation of a cell decomposition (general-position normalisation)

ideas.what: Viewing the move in configuration space X as an 'anti-sweep' of a wall s of the discriminant Σ.
ideas.modern_name: wall-crossing in the stratified space of arrangements / discriminantal arrangement
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses tame topology and stratified spaces in general, not this

ideas.what: Gluing the polygons Δ_L and Δ_{L'} along corresponding transition arcs (via the s↔t symmetry) to get a 2-complex with quadrilateral faces dual to the graph of relative positions.
ideas.modern_name: cellular model of the flip graph; compare rhombic/zonotopal tilings dual to pseudoline arrangements (Bohne–Dress) and the 2-cells of higher Bruhat orders
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bohne–Dress (1992); Manin–Schechtman; Kapranov–Voevodsky (1994) for the 2-categorical side

missed.claim: A program to build a cell complex out of the structural polygons Δ_L of a single pseudoline, glued along corresponding generalization/specialization arcs, modelling the space of relative positions. Its links with the flip-graph and zonotopal-tiling literature are not worked out here.
missed.quote: si (L,a) et (L',a') ... se correspondent, il est utile d'attacher Δ_L et Δ_{L'}, par identification
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an alternative, line-centred combinatorial model of the cell structure of pseudoline-arrangement spaces. That is relevant to higher Bruhat orders and to contractibility questions for flip complexes. Whether it differs substantively from known constructions is unclear from this page alone.

deep.surprise_reason: The page carefully redevelops known pseudoline combinatorics (triangle flips, crossing order along a line) in Grothendieck's own idiom, plus a technical normalisation. The gluing of the Δ_L polygons is a mildly original construction, but it is only begun here and seems close to known dual/tiling pictures.
transcription_corrections: Middle passage should read roughly: 'Le bénéfice, c'est que les arcs de transition sont 2 à 2 mutuellement disjoints dans tous les cas, et que deux arcs caractéristiques rétractés adjacents ont une et une seule extrémité (au sens "rétracté"), et ceci sans avoir à faire d'exceptions.'
'en jouant par lui de sorte antipodalique' more likely reads '... de cet arc, et (par là) de son antipodique, censés d'être arcs de généralisation'.
'pris comme pas changé' likely 'censé pas changé' / 'supposé non changé'.
'Il peut être commode de l'éloigner' is uncertain; it may be 'de l'élaguer' / 'de le rétrécir' (the sense is shrinking the arc).
'les arcs de généralisation servent : origines' should read 'servent d'origines à une opération de généralisation'.
After 'antibalayage' the underlined word is illegible ('glissement' is a guess; it could be 'décalage').
